resolutions.corridor_desc: Western Desert — a short (10 km) Khalda-operated discovery tie-in.
resolutions.researcher_notes: IDENTITY CONFIRMED, GEOMETRY NOT. Two independent sources (tradearabia.com, gulfnews.com) identify Wanda as a July-2026 Khalda Petroleum discovery tie-in, and both quote a $2.3M cost over 10 km — matching GEM's own Cost and LengthKnownKm exactly, which corroborates the row itself. Neither source, nor any other found this session, gives coordinates for the Wanda well or for the receiving facility, and 'Wanda' returns no gazetteer hit. Existence is well sourced; geometry is not obtainable from public sources.

resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN — one end only. The Abu Gharadig end is pinned at medium confidence (28.5611/29.7927, the Abu Gharadig field/processing area). The NORPETCO / North Bahariya end could not be geocoded at all: none of the concession's named development leases (Abrar, Ferdaus, Ganna, Rawda, Rayan, Sidra) returns a gazetteer or OSM hit, and no source gives the tie-in point. A one-ended corridor cannot be drawn without inventing the other end.

resolutions.corridor_desc: Fayoum / Beni Suef / Giza — unclear; the row's own name may be a mis-transcription.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and the row's identity is in question. No pipeline named 'Fayoum-Giza' was found in any source. The closest real project is Ministry of Petroleum Decision 1884/2025, a three-line 40.5 km distribution buildout in Fayoum, whose 19 km Beni Suef-New Fayoum segment runs parallel to the 'Giza Canal' (ترعة الجيزة) — the likely origin of the 'Giza' fragment in this row's name. Geometry aside, the name is arithmetically inconsistent with the row: Fayoum city to Giza city is 60-70 km against a sheet length of 27.0 km. Routes to Update as a naming/identity question before any route work.

resolutions.start_name: SUMED Pipelines Terminal, Ain Sokhna, Suez Governorate (Red Sea / Gulf of Suez coast)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Ain Sokhna, Suez Governorate — a 6.1 km spur from the SUMED terminal into GASCO's national grid.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN — one end only, but this pass SETTLES the landfall question four prior passes left open. The Ministry of Petroleum's own magazine (petro-mag.org, Nov 2025, GASCO feature) reads 'خط استيراد الغاز من ميناء سوميد بالعين السخنة' — 'gas import line from the SUMED port AT AIN SOKHNA' — so the terminal is Ain Sokhna on the Red Sea, NOT Sidi Kerir on the Mediterranean. Start pinned high (32.3226725/29.6001749). The grid-side tie-in has never been named in any source, in this pass or the four before it; Ain Sokhna hosts several GASCO compressor/metering facilities 5-8 km out, geographically consistent with 6.1 km, but picking one without a source would be fabrication. TWO items for Update: (a) GEM's pipeline NAME here collides with SUMED's own crude-OIL pipeline name — a naming collision in GEM's data, not evidence of a different route; (b) the World Bank ESIA cited in this row's Status [ref] (SFG1795-EA-P116194) verifies live but is about the GIZA NORTH power station, an unrelated project — it is not route corroboration for this line.

resolutions.start_name: Sonker terminal area, Ain Sokhna port (general port-area proxy — no mappable 'Sonker' feature exists)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Ain Sokhna port — Sonker terminal to an unnamed GASCO grid tie-in. SHARED with P8007.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN. Sonker is a private terminal operator at Ain Sokhna; petro-mag.org (Nov 2025) places a Sonker gas offtake line there at Phase 1, 9 km, gas flowing 10 Jul 2025 — matching GEM's 9.0 km EXACTLY — but names neither the jetty structure nor the grid tie-in, and no map or GIS source names 'Sonker' at all. The start coordinate is a port-area proxy, not a facility. IMPORTANT for whoever draws these: P8006 (Phase 1) and P8007 (Phase 2) are geographically INDISTINGUISHABLE — no source describes them as following different corridors; they are sequential capacity phases of one Sonker-to-grid connection. If geometry is ever drawn, the honest representation is ONE corridor flagged as shared by both PIDs, never two distinct paths presented as separately confirmed.

LENGTH CONFLICT for Update, carried here so it travels with the endpoint work: GEM's sheet says 7.0 km, petro-mag.org says 8 km for the same phase — already flagged in notes/review-2026-07-28-na-egypt-gas-additions.md and NOT resolved by this pass, since no independent second source gives a Phase 2 length.

resolutions.corridor_desc: North Sinai — a 15.5 km sub-segment somewhere within the Bir al-Abd → El Arish Abr Sinai corridor.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and deliberately so: the corridor is well sourced but this PID's own span is not. 'Abr Sinai II' is the second duplication of GASCO's Trans-Sinai line; GEM's already-mapped P8044 is the first (EIB-financed 2007-09, Bir al-Abd → El Arish). A 2007 EIB EIA independently corroborates that P8044 route — the chord between the two named places computes to ~75.8 km against the EIA's stated ~78 km along-road. But P8008 is 15.5 km (gas flowed 8 Jun 2024 per petro-mag.org, the only source found for this row), i.e. roughly a fifth of that corridor, and NO source names which km-range it covers. The Bir al-Abd and El Arish coordinates are sourced CORRIDOR BOUNDS, valid in their own right; assigning either as this segment's endpoint would overstate what is known, so they are recorded as context only and no coordinates are staged. Hypothesis for a future pass, explicitly NOT a finding: the EIB project's own 'Loop 1'/'Loop 2' structure suggests 'Pipeline 1' (completed first) may be the shorter Loop-1 stretch near El-Tena East/Qantara — pattern-matching on naming, nothing more.

resolutions.corridor_desc: North Sinai — a 27 km sub-segment within the same Bir al-Abd → El Arish Abr Sinai corridor as P8008; El Arish end weakly favoured.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN — same corridor and same limits as P8008 (see its note for the corridor and chord math). 27 km (sheet, matching petro-mag.org Nov 2025) vs 28 km (Dec 2024 issue) is an internal magazine inconsistency already flagged in a prior pass and not resolved here; either way it is far short of the ~75.8 km full corridor, so this is a partial stretch. WEAK circumstantial support for the El Arish end: an Akhbar El-Yom article of 7 Apr 2026 reports GASCO negotiating farmer compensation for 'the second phase' (المرحلة الثانية) of the 'Sinai gas pipeline duplication' (ازدواج خط الغاز عبر سيناء) with Arish's own Agricultural Administration — so land acquisition for something called phase 2 was active near Arish in April 2026. The article never uses a PID or 'Pipeline 2' terminology and gives no coordinates, so confidence stays low and no endpoint is staged. SEE ALSO the P8055 duplicate question.

resolutions.corridor_desc: North Sinai — a 28 km duplication stretch of the Trans-Sinai/Abr Sinai line; endpoints unnamed in every source.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and this row has a bigger problem than its geometry. SOURCE RECOVERED -- CORRECTION to this pass's earlier reading. All seven of its [ref] cells cite one GASCO PDF whose URL as filed 404s, and this pass first called that a genuine deletion. WITHDRAWN: the document is LIVE. The filed filename hyphenates what are really spaces -- the real URL is https://www.gasco.com.eg/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/National%20Natural%20Gas%20Grid%20Expansion%20Projects.pdf (200, 77,826 bytes, application/pdf; url_verifier ok=True with insecure_tls, i.e. incomplete cert chain but live). The 404 on the hyphenated form is honest (a nonsense sibling returns the same 196-byte body), and Wayback capture 20260222074837 holds the space form. So NOTHING here needs re-sourcing: it is a URL correction on 8 cells (P8055 x7 + P6685 ProjectLevelCost [ref]). The document is GASCO's own Dec-2024 project register: length, diameter, governorate, cost in BOTH EGP and USD, status and completion date per project. LIKELY DUPLICATE OF P8009 -- flagged for human adjudication, NOT merged, and now decidable: the register lists EXACTLY ONE Trans-Sinai duplication (28 km, 36 in, Sinai, 631 M EGP / 13 M USD, 'Under Study'), and P8055 matches it to the cell including its 13,000,000 USD ProjectLevelCost -- this row IS that table row. P8009 (27.00 km, 36 in) is the same project as reported by petro-mag.org, the 27-vs-28 gap being that magazine's own Nov-2025-vs-Dec-2024 inconsistency. IF FOLDED, P8009's STATUS SHOULD SURVIVE: P8055's 'proposed' faithfully reflects a Dec-2024 source, but the Ministry of Petroleum grid document lists the duplication under CONSTRUCTION, and an Akhbar El-Yom report of 7 Apr 2026 has GASCO negotiating farmer compensation for 'the second phase' near Arish -- one project that moved Under Study -> construction, carried as two rows. Carry P8055's sourced cost and the corrected URL onto the survivor. P8008 does NOT fold (15.5 km, gas flowed 8 Jun 2024). Routing to Update. Geometry unchanged: still NOT DRAWN -- no source gives this line's endpoints or km-range along the P8044 corridor. See notes/escalation-2026-08-27-egypt-gas-trans-sinai-cluster-and-p3931.md

resolutions.corridor_desc: Merged Meleiha concession, Western Desert (Matrouh/Alexandria desert road area) — an in-field gathering network, not a point-to-point trunk.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and a point-to-point model does not fit. The sheet's start and end coordinates are IDENTICAL (27.1108/30.7753), and three independent sources describe this as a gas GATHERING NETWORK inside the Merged Meleiha concession (IEOC/Agiba operatorship) rather than a trunk between two named places. A 130 km gathering system has no two endpoints to draw between; a great-circle line would misrepresent its physical form. Needs either an operator schematic or field-by-field wellpad anchors, neither of which is public. Flagging the identical start/end coordinates as a separate data question.

resolutions.corridor_desc: Qena Governorate, Upper Egypt — a short spur between a gas pressure-reduction/pumping station and Qena city.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN. No distinct 'Qena P.S.' could be located as a place separate from Qena city: every gazetteer and OSM query collapses both ends onto the Qena city centroid (OSM node 299501065), which would make a zero-length line against a sheet length of 8.0 km. One lead — an Al-Ahram Gate item naming a gas pressure-reduction station 'in Qena city' — 403s at the origin (a block, not a deletion) and its Wayback capture 20260213140557 was unreachable this session; flagged for a retry pass, not cited. Drawing Qena→Qena would be fabricated geometry, not an imprecise one.

resolutions.start_name: Kima (KIMA chemical/fertilizer complex settlement), Aswan Governorate
resolutions.researcher_notes: Sourced endpoints: kimaegypt.com (official KIMA project page, live) confirms the plant's Aswan-Governorate location and its 1.2 Mm3/d @ 25 bar gas requirement delivered via a filtration/reduction plant; ammoniaenergy.org (live) independently states gas reaches KIMA at Aswan by pipeline from the north via Assiut; youm7.com (live) reports gas reaching Aswan governorate in 2009 as KIMA's lifeline. Tier: medium (corroborated corridor, 2+ independent sources on existence, none on geometry).

proposed_sheet.RouteNotes: Straight-line corridor between two independently sourced named endpoints: the KIMA industrial complex at Kima, Aswan Governorate, and Aswan city. Great-circle 4.24 km vs sheet length 4.0 km (+6%). Endpoint coordinates are OSM place/way centroids (way/98332273 for Kima; node/1667671341 for Aswan city), not surveyed plant-gate or station points. No source gives literal pipeline coordinates; corroborated corridor only. See P8073 for the open identity/length question between these two Aswan-Kima records.

resolutions.corridor_desc: Aswan Governorate — Aswan city to the KIMA industrial complex, the same corridor as P8072.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and it raises a prior question. Anchoring returned exactly the same two named places as P8072 (Kima settlement, OSM way/98332273; Aswan city, OSM node/1667671341), 4.24 km apart — against this row's sheet length of 20.0 km, a ~4.7x mismatch. The High Dam was tested as an alternative Aswan-end anchor and rejected (11.9 km, still well short). So either (a) P8072 'Kima Aswan Industrial' and P8073 'Aswan-Kima' are two records of one pipeline and one of the two lengths is wrong, or (b) P8073 is a longer feeder from somewhere north of Aswan city that no source names. Reusing P8072's geometry here would invent a 4.2 km line for a 20 km row and manufacture a false corroboration between two rows that may be duplicates. Routes to Update as a duplicate/length question, not to Route Creation.

resolutions.start_name: Abu Sultan Power Station (محطة كهرباء أبو سلطان البخارية), Ismailia Governorate — East Delta Electricity Production Company
resolutions.end_name: Shabab Power Station (محطة كهرباء الشباب), near Tell El Kebir, Ismailia Governorate — East Delta Electricity Production Company
resolutions.researcher_notes: Endpoints rung of the source ladder, accuracy 'low' — a two-vertex chord, not a surveyed route. The real pipe will follow the Ismailia Canal / Lake Timsah corridor rather than this straight line, so treat the geometry as a corridor placeholder pending a traced route. 'El Shabab' in GEM's name is the Shabab power station, not a generic term: almalnews.com's 2024 GASCO roundup independently names الشباب as one of GASCO's four P.R.M. stations. A contractor page (civecon.com, Petrojet-affiliated) was seen during research explicitly describing an 'Abu Sultan - Shabab Power Plant' gas pipeline project, which would be a third independent corroboration, but the specific project URL could not be re-located and re-verified, so per the no-fabricated-URL rule it is deliberately NOT cited.

proposed_sheet.RouteNotes: Straight-line corridor between two sourced endpoints. Start = Abu Sultan power station (600 MW, gas-fired, in service 1983); end = Shabab power station (1,500 MW combined-cycle), both East Delta Electricity Production Company assets in Ismailia Governorate, both reported in EEHC's own annual report (moee.gov.eg EEHC_Rep 2017-2018) and both carrying separate Wikidata entries; coordinates geocoded from OSM (ways 105569177 and 124777337), the Abu Sultan point independently cross-checked against a separately-queried OSM landuse=industrial feature 30 m away. Great-circle separation 37.4 km vs the sheet's 38.0 km (98.4%).

The pair was re-derived independently here rather than inherited: start from OSM way 352862333 with WDGC's El-Amreya co-location confirmed by GASCO's own gas-plants page (1997 establishment, May 2000 startup, co-located Amerya LPG recovery plant); end from OSM way 352865112, tagged name=MIDOR, industrial=refinery, operator=EGPC, with MIDOR's own site confirming the Amreya Free Zone address. resolutions.start_name: Al-Ma'addiyyah / Boughaz El-Maadia channel at the Lake Idku outlet, near Idku, Beheira Governorate
resolutions.researcher_notes: ONE ITEM FOR UPDATE: the sheet's Start governorate reads 'Damietta', but Al-Ma'addiyyah is at the Idku outlet in BEHEIRA — as is the End (Damanhur). Both ends are Beheira. Not silently corrected; flagged for adjudication. 'Meadia' is a channel, not a governorate or major town, which is the likely origin of the mis-entry. Only one precise-coordinate source exists for the start anchor (the OSM node), so its confidence is medium, not high.

proposed_sheet.RouteNotes: Schematic chord between sourced endpoints. 'Meadia' in GEM's name is a transliteration of Al-Ma'addiyyah, the channel connecting Lake Idku to Abu Qir Bay — identified from OSM node 768567336 (قلعة المعدية) with the channel's identity and function independently confirmed in Wikipedia's Idku article, which gives no coordinate of its own. End = Damanhur (Wikipedia infobox, corroborated by GeoNames within ~200 m). Chord 38.6 km against the sheet's 50.0 km (ratio 0.77): expected, since the real corridor must skirt Lake Idku and the Abu Qir wetlands rather than cross them — which is also why this is staged schematic rather than 'low'.

resolutions.end_name: Damanhur, capital of Beheira Governorate (Wikipedia infobox, corroborated by GeoNames within ~200 m)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Alexandria Governorate → Damanhur, Beheira — 45 km from an UNIDENTIFIED take-off point on GASCO's Alexandria-area grid.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN, and the length check is why. The pipeline is real and independently named: an Egypt Oil & Gas feature (Wood Mackenzie-sourced) lists 'Alexandria Network-Damanhur' alongside 'Meadia-Damanhur' and 'Abu Madi-Damietta' in the same grid taxonomy, so this is not a GEM-only name. But 'Alexandria Network' names GASCO's whole Alexandria-area distribution grid, not one facility, so there is no named take-off point to anchor — and Alexandria city centre is provably the WRONG anchor: the chord from either published city point to Damanhur is 55.8-57.8 km, LONGER than the sheet's 45.0 km, which no real corridor can be. (Wikipedia and GeoNames disagree by ~2 km on where 'Alexandria' is, which is itself the point.) So the true take-off is measurably closer to Damanhur — Kafr El Dawwar, an industrial town roughly midway, is the obvious candidate corridor but is NOT sourced and is explicitly not staged as a finding. The end anchor (Damanhur) is solid and recorded. This row's WebSearch budget ran out mid-task; it is the one row in this batch that a fresh pass with Arabic-language search ('شبكة الاسكندرية' city-gate / take-off station) has a real chance of closing. Sheet governorates (Alexandria → Beheira) are plausible and NOT flagged.

resolutions.end_name: 10th of Ramadan City, Sharqia Governorate (CITY CENTROID, not the P.R.M. station itself)
resolutions.corridor_desc: Sharqia Governorate — a 4.5 km spur from an unnamed national-grid tie-in to the 10th of Ramadan city-gate/P.R.M. station.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN. The pipeline's IDENTITY is well corroborated by two independent live sources: GASCO's own gas-grid page confirms the 10th of Ramadan concession is fed by GASCO lines of 2-16 in (matching GEM's 16 in), and almalnews.com (2024) lists خط غاز العاشر من رمضان among GASCO's completed national-grid reinforcement projects while separately naming العاشر من رمضان as one of GASCO's four P.R.M. (pressure-reduction and measurement) stations. What does not exist publicly is a named ORIGIN: no source in Arabic or English — GASCO's site, Ministry of Petroleum reporting, the presidency.eg project database, or OSM — names which trunk this 4.5 km spur taps. OSM has zero mapped pipeline infrastructure in the bounding box, so even the destination anchor is a city centroid rather than the station. A short tie-in from a Sharqia branch of the national grid is the plausible reading and is explicitly NOT staged as a finding. Note the destination coordinate is city-level: do not treat it as station-precise if this row is drawn later.

resolutions.end_name: Cairo West Power Plant (محطة كهرباء غرب القاهرة), Cairo Electricity Production Company — OSM way 807008190
resolutions.corridor_desc: Greater Cairo — 16 km / 30 in feed line from an unnamed national-grid origin west of Cairo to the Cairo West power station.
resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT DRAWN — one end only, but this pass RESOLVES what the name means. 'P.S.' here is POWER STATION, not pressure station, settled by an exact government project match: the Egyptian presidency's project database (read via the egy-map.com mirror, since presidency.eg itself 403s a scraper) carries إنشاء خط تغذية محطة كهرباء غرب القاهرة — a 16 km, 30-inch line to feed the West Cairo power station with gas, completed June 2020 at 403 million EGP. That is an exact match to GEM's length, diameter, date and purpose, independently corroborated by almalnews.com's 2024 GASCO roundup (تغذية محطتى كهرباء الوليدية وغرب القاهرة). So identity, length, diameter, cost and destination are unusually well sourced; only the geometry is open. No source names the ORIGIN / grid tie-in — the government record gives specs and destination, never a from/to pair. ONE ITEM FOR UPDATE: the destination plant sits in GIZA governorate per both OSM's own tagging and the operator's site (cairoepc.com: تقع المحطة سقيل - الجيزة), while GEM files the row under Cairo at both ends — mirroring the government database's own Cairo filing. That is a real sourced discrepancy; the likely reading is that the corridor runs through Cairo territory to a terminus at or just past the boundary, but it is recorded as an open question, not resolved.
